Yes — the closest match is MoCo Rubric, which uses a single shared vision-language model for the caption policy, rubric generator, and rubric judge, and updates the generator and judge with an exponential moving average of the policy parameters [1]. It is designed for detailed image captioning and uses rubric-based rewards to improve factual accuracy, information coverage, and clarity [1].

The other papers are less direct matches: one focuses on evaluating specificity versus length in image descriptions [2], and another uses a judge-corrector pipeline for multimodal machine translation rather than captioning [5].
